items.finding: Temperature is identified as a factor that can strongly affect NIR model performance, because shifts in the water absorbance bands with temperature can reduce model performance.
items.how_it_applies: This is a reason to measure temperature at the sample point (as in O2) and to test how temperature variation across the expected process range affects the water model. A first comparison experiment could include spectra at several temperatures to check for band shifts.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The finding concerns NIR spectra of kiwifruit juice, not mid-IR spectra of petroleum, so the magnitude and direction of temperature effects may differ. It is a published sensitivity observation, not evidence that any specific sensor or compensation approach works for this stream.

citation.quote: A factor that can strongly affect NIR model performance is temperature [8]. Shifts in the water absorbance bands with temperature can reduce model performance [9,10,11,12].
citation.label: E03 ¶3

items.finding: In the studied juice, increasing temperature mainly caused a lateral wavelength shift in the first overtone region and a vertical amplitude shift in the second overtone region of water.
items.how_it_applies: It suggests concrete spectral signatures of temperature influence (wavelength and amplitude shifts of water bands) that a comparison experiment could look for when varying temperature at the measurement point.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: Derived from NIR overtone regions of water in kiwifruit juice; petroleum matrices and mid-IR methods may show different temperature behaviour. It does not quantify any accuracy or detection limit.

citation.quote: The influence of increasing temperature on the peak absorbance of the juice was largely a lateral wavelength shift in the first overtone region and a vertical amplitude shift in the second overtone region of water.
citation.label: E03 ¶1
